name: Mangrove
notes: Intertidal salt-tolerant forest: stilt-rooted Rhizophora on the seaward edge, pneumatophore-bearing Avicennia/Sonneratia, Laguncularia/Bruguiera landward, nipa palm and ferns at the freshwater fringe. Drawn on the Atlantic-East Pacific (Florida, Caribbean, W Africa) and Indo-West Pacific (Sundarbans, SE Asia, N Australia) mangrove provinces.

canopy.name: Black mangrove

bark.note: dark grey to black, fissured into small scaly plates; inner bark orange

canopy.silhouette: grey-green rounded crown over a pencil-root field

growth.juvenile_note: Cryptoviviparous: the embryo germinates inside the fruit on the tree. A stranded propagule sheds its skin, opens two thick, folded, fleshy green cotyledons like a butterfly and anchors with a hairy radicle. The seedling is a slender single stem with opposite, leathery, narrow leaves, grey-hairy beneath; pencil-like pneumatophores soon ring the young tree.
growth.source: USDA Tropical Tree Seed Manual, Avicennia germinans (14-20 m, young trees add ~60 cm/yr, viviparous, propagules float >4 months); Useful Tropical Plants (seedlings 26 cm at 4 months); first flowering age and lifespan estimated.

fruiting.source: USDA Tropical Tree Seed Manual (flowers May-Jul, white with yellow base, nectar-rich honey flowers, flattened 2-valved capsule, propagules peak Sep-Oct); Useful Tropical Plants (cotyledons eaten in famine after careful preparation); flower life, fruit set and crop estimated.

canopy.name: Coconut palm

growth.juvenile_note: The husked nut lies on the sand and after 2-6 months a pointed shoot pushes out of one end while the nut's flesh feeds the seedling. First leaves are entire, stiff, strap-like blades split only at the tip (bifid), in a stemless fan-like rosette; pinnate fronds come later, and a trunk rises after ~3-5 years, widening from a bulbous base ('bole').
growth.source: Wikipedia Coconut (tall palms bear at 6-10 yr, live 60-100 yr; ~11 months from female flower opening to harvest; up to 15 inflorescences/yr; ~80 nuts/yr, up to 150; nut ~1.4 kg; largely cross-pollinated, dwarfs selfing); ICRAF Agroforestree (tall selections 24-30 m, flowers after ~6th yr); germination from FAO coconut guides

canopy.source: Palm of tropical coasts worldwide; height 15-30 m. Leaning trunk, feather crown; sea-dispersed nuts. Standard floras and Kew POWO for the name.

traits.petiole: long fibrous petiole with a leaf sheath

bark.note: grey-brown trunk ringed with leaf scars

canopy.silhouette: leaning ringed pole with arching feather fronds

fruiting.source: Wikipedia Coconut and ICRAF (new inflorescence among the leaves every ~3-4 weeks, up to 15/yr, thousands of small male flowers and ~20-50 large 25 mm female flowers per inflorescence; cross-pollinated by insects and wind; ~11-12 months to a mature brown nut that drops; 50-150 nuts per palm per year)

growth.juvenile_note: Viviparous: the seed sprouts on the tree and a green, pencil-like hypocotyl 20-30 cm long hangs from the brown fruit. It drops, floats (weeks, up to a year), lodges upright in mud, roots from the lower tip within days and opens a pair of glossy leaves at the top. The sapling is a single stem that soon throws down arching red-brown prop roots.
growth.source: Tropical Plants Database (theferns.info) Rhizophora mangle (1-1.5 m/yr on productive sites; 5-20 m, rarely 30; flowers year-round; flowering by 6 yr, even 3-5 yr at 0.5-1 m tall; propagules 8-30 cm); Wikipedia (to 24 m, commonly ~6 m; propagules may float over a year); lifespan and shade estimated

fruiting.source: Wikipedia (white bell-shaped flowers ~5 mm in spikes; flattened, ridged reddish-brown drupe 12-20 mm, water-dispersed). Flowering season (spring-summer in Florida and the Caribbean), pollinators, timings and counts estimated.

shrub.name: Sea oxeye
shrub.origin: SE US, Mexico and Caribbean coasts

growth.juvenile_note: Seedlings are uncommon; most new plants are shoots from the running rhizomes of an existing colony. A young shoot is a single upright stem with pairs of thick, silvery-grey, hairy, spoon-shaped leaves; it branches little, turns woody at the base and is soon one of many stems in a dense, knee- to waist-high grey patch topped by yellow daisies.
growth.source: Flora of North America vol. 21 (Borrichia frutescens: rhizomatous colonial shrub 10-120(-200) cm; leaves opposite, obovate to oblanceolate, sericeous; heads solitary, rays yellow; salt marshes, mangrove margins and coastal flats); establishment mostly clonal; timings estimated.

repro.note: spreads mainly by rhizomes into clonal colonies; heads visited by bees and butterflies; the corky achenes float

shrub.source: Borrichia frutescens, sea oxeye: silvery-leaved colonial subshrub 0.3-1.2 m of salt-marsh edges, mangrove margins and salt flats, Virginia to Texas, Mexico, Bermuda and the West Indies — Flora of North America vol. 21; Odum et al. 1982 (landward mangrove fringe). Kew POWO for the name.

growth.juvenile_note: Seedlings are rare (germination is episodic, needing fresh water on saline ground); the seedling is a small tuft of short, stiff, grey-green leaves in two neat opposite ranks. Scaly rhizomes then run through the soil and send up rows of short, stiff, leafy shoots, forming a dense, low turf patch; male and female plants are separate.
growth.source: USDA FEIS Distichlis spicata (dioecious; seeds need stratification and scarification, germination rare and episodic, seedling survival 0-95% with falling salinity; rhizomes to 180 cm long, 10-25 cm deep; 15-45 cm tall, usually <30 cm; photosynthesis rises with light). Time to flowering and clone lifespan estimated.

ground.name: Shoregrass

growth.juvenile_note: A seedling is a tiny tuft of short, stiff, needle-like grey-green leaves. It soon throws out wiry stolons that run over the bare salt flat and root at every node, each node carrying a little cluster of the same short, sharp leaves, until the plant knits a low, springy, grey-green mat that reddens in drought.
growth.source: Flora of North America vol. 25 (as Monanthochloe littoralis: stoloniferous mat-forming dioecious perennial, culms 3-20 cm, blades 3-10 mm, subulate, glaucous, clustered at the nodes; coastal salt flats and marsh edges, Florida and Texas to the Caribbean and Mexico); timings estimated.

repro.note: dioecious; spreads mostly by rooting stolons; flowers hidden among the leaf clusters

growth.source: Flora of North America vol. 25 (Paspalum vaginatum: rhizomatous and stoloniferous perennial, culms 10-79 cm, blades 2-15 cm x 2-8 mm, racemes usually 2, paired; brackish shores, tidal flats and ditches); timings estimated.

epiphyte.name: Strangler fig

growth.juvenile_note: Usually starts as a bird-dropped seed in a palm boot or branch fork: a tiny leafy shrublet perched on the host, with glossy oval leaves, that sends thin aerial roots down the trunk. Once they reach soil the roots thicken and fuse into a lattice that strangles the host; it can also start on the ground or on rocks as a normal sapling.
growth.source: Wikipedia (Ficus aurea: hemiepiphytic strangler to 30 m that germinates in the host canopy; fast-growing). Germination, ages and lifespan estimated from Ficus.

epiphyte.source: Florida and Caribbean hammocks. Starts in a crown, sends roots down, kills the host — a real strangler event on old trees. Kew POWO.
